_comment: Checks the case-eligibility criterion: survivors are not a fair sample of all cases.

stem.en: A surgeon offers a case-control study all the patients with a rare cancer who still attend his clinic, some of them diagnosed 12 years ago. Why is a series of newly diagnosed patients usually better?

text.en: The old cases are the ones who survived, so they may differ from patients who died soon after diagnosis
The old cases are more likely to remember their past exposure accurately
Newly diagnosed patients are always younger than long-term patients
Patients diagnosed years ago cannot be matched to controls of the same age

explanation.en: A patient who is still attending years after diagnosis has survived, and survival may be related to the exposure being studied. Such old, prevalent cases are not a fair sample of everyone who develops the disease, so a fixed period of newly diagnosed cases is preferred.

hints.en: Ask what had to happen to a patient for that patient to be in the clinic 12 years later.
